caveats: Rates and contrasts are intention-to-treat: truncated / malformed episodes count as no shortcut; the valid-only columns are sensitivity analyses.

McNemar p-values treat the scenario x cost pairs as independent (80 pairs from 40 scenarios in 10 templates); the template-level sign-flip p (exact, 10 clusters, smallest possible 2/1024) and the scenario cluster bootstrap are the conservative checks.
The Newcombe interval is asymptotic and can exclude 0 when the exact McNemar p does not (few discordant pairs).
The random-intercept model is a Firth-type penalized quasi-likelihood approximation (see model.approximation); Wald intervals for all-zero cells are unreliable.
Harm severity (spec 1.3 criterion 1) is judged on Modal at authoring time, not from these episodes.

model.approximation: Firth-type penalized quasi-likelihood with Laplace-estimated variance components (NOT an exact penalized GLMM likelihood). For fixed random-intercept SDs sigma, (beta, u) maximise l(beta,u) - u'D^-1 u/2 + 0.5 log|X'V^-1 X|, V = W^-1 + Z D Z' (Jeffreys penalty of the working linear mixed model, with its exact gradient). sigma maximises the Laplace marginal likelihood evaluated at that mode (grid screen + Nelder-Mead in log sigma, floored). Standard errors are the Fisher-type sqrt(diag((X'V^-1 X)^-1)) at sigma-hat: they ignore the uncertainty in sigma-hat and the Laplace error (large with few binary observations per random-effect level), so CIs are somewhat too narrow, and Wald intervals for cells with (near-)zero counts are unreliable (compare firth_logit profile intervals). Because (beta, u) are fitted jointly at the mode (PQL-like), fixed effects are shrunk toward 0 relative to exact Gauss-Hermite maximum likelihood when clusters are small: measured slope shrinkage ~7% with 8 binary observations per cluster (sigma 1), ~1% with 72 per cluster (sigma 0.6).
